questions.stem: The minister's remarks were later ____ as misinterpreted, but the damage was done.
questions.explanation: Retracted = withdrawn formally; that fits 'misinterpreted' + 'but the damage was done'. Reaffirmed = said again (opposite). Refined = improved. Regarded = considered.

questions.topic: Cloze test / fill-blank II — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Due to the storm, the flight was ____ by three hours.
questions.explanation: Delayed — postponed / held back. Deluded = deceived. Depleted = used up. Denied = refused. Flights commonly get 'delayed'.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Cloze test / fill-blank II — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The report contains ____ evidence of the company's wrongdoing, making litigation inevitable.
questions.explanation: Incontrovertible = impossible to deny / indisputable → strongest form of evidence → 'making litigation inevitable' makes sense. Circumstantial = indirect. Incoherent = illogical. Inconsequential = unimportant.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Cloze test / fill-blank II — mixed tiers

questions.stem: She was able to ____ her fears and deliver an excellent presentation.
questions.explanation: Overcome fears — to conquer or succeed despite fears. Aggravate = make worse. Invite = ask to come. Envisage = imagine as future.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Cloze test / fill-blank II — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Globalisation has led to an ____ flow of goods, services and ideas across borders.
questions.explanation: Unprecedented = never done/known before. Intermittent = occasional. Context 'globalisation' → implies dramatic, never-before-seen scale → unprecedented is the best collocation.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Cloze test / fill-blank II — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The new law will ____ the existing regulations on waste management.
questions.explanation: Supersede = replace / take the place of (especially an older rule). Succumb = yield. Suspend = stop temporarily. Suspect = doubt. A NEW law supersedes old regulations.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Cloze test / fill-blank II — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The judge, known for his ____ intellect, unravelled the complex case within days.
questions.explanation: Incisive = sharply analytical, cutting through confusion. 'Unravelled... within days' needs sharp + fast thinking. Mundane = ordinary. Muddled = confused. Mediocre = average.

questions.stem: Despite working for twelve hours straight, the construction workers showed no signs of ____; they pressed on with the same vigour.

options.option_text: sudden anger or irritability at supervisors

questions.explanation: D is correct because the contrast marker 'despite' and the phrase 'pressed on with the same vigour' signal that 'fatigue/exhaustion' is the expected outcome they surprisingly avoided. A (confusion) is irrelevant to prolonged physical labour. B (happiness) and C (anger) both contradict the neutral-to-positive 'vigour' mentioned in the latter clause.

questions.stem: The relief workers ____ essential supplies among the flood victims in a calm and orderly manner.

options.option_text: carefully withheld the essentials from all
methodically distributed the goods to each

questions.explanation: C is correct because relief workers 'distribute' supplies to victims — the phrase 'orderly manner' reinforces a systematic, giving action. A (withheld) is the exact opposite of relief work. B (collected donations from bystanders) reverses the direction of aid. D (demanded resources) misrepresents relief workers as antagonists rather than helpers.

questions.stem: The new CEO's vision was ____; she transformed not just the company's balance sheet but its entire organisational culture.

options.option_text: remarkably narrow and one-dimensional in scope
surprisingly cautious and risk-averse at every stage
deliberately vague and open to multiple interpretations

questions.explanation: B is correct because transforming both finances AND culture simultaneously signals a wide-ranging, all-encompassing vision — best captured by 'comprehensive and far-reaching.' A (narrow) directly contradicts the breadth described. C (cautious) conflicts with the bold double transformation. D (vague) would imply no clear direction, contradicting concrete outcomes mentioned.

questions.stem: The scientist refused to ____ her findings even when senior colleagues publicly questioned her methodology.
questions.explanation: A is correct because 'refused to retract' means she stood firmly by her results under pressure — a meaning reinforced by the adversarial 'even when senior colleagues questioned her.' B (promote) changes the action entirely. C (revise) implies cooperative updating rather than resistance. D (defend) is tempting but she refused to 'defend' makes no logical sense — one refuses to retract, not to defend.

questions.stem: The author's prose was so ____ that readers often had to revisit passages multiple times to fully grasp their meaning.

options.option_text: deliberately simple and easy to comprehend

questions.explanation: D is correct because needing to 're-read passages multiple times to grasp meaning' is a hallmark of dense, complex prose. A (simple/easy) is the direct opposite. B (brief) contradicts 'passages' implying extended, elaborate writing. C (emotional) is irrelevant to comprehension difficulty — an emotional text can be perfectly clear; complexity of syntax is what demands re-reading.

questions.stem: His argument, though ____ on the surface, concealed several logical fallacies that only a discerning reader would identify.
questions.explanation: C is correct because 'though ___ on the surface' paired with 'concealed fallacies' demands a word conveying deceptive plausibility — 'superficially persuasive' fits precisely. A (logically rigorous) would mean no fallacies exist at all, contradicting the sentence. B (overtly flawed) contradicts 'on the surface' — if flaws are overt, they need not be concealed. D (deliberately ambiguous) implies the author intended obscurity, not flawed-but-convincing reasoning.

questions.stem: The activist's speech was remarkable for its ____ quality — she challenged the administration forcefully without ever descending into incendiary rhetoric.

options.option_text: overtly aggressive and confrontational rhetorical style
measured yet incisive and critically penetrating
deliberately evasive and carefully non-committal stance
excessively deferential and apologetically mild manner

questions.explanation: B is correct because 'measured yet incisive' captures speech that is controlled in tone yet sharp in substance — exactly consistent with 'challenged forcefully without descending into rhetoric.' A (aggressive/confrontational) is directly negated by 'without ever descending into incendiary rhetoric.' C (evasive/non-committal) contradicts 'challenged forcefully.' D (deferential/mild) contradicts any meaningful challenge to authority.
